title: On-prem Audit Forwarder: resilient uploads, per-tenant CMEK, and lifecycle policies
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
Build the next-generation on-prem/VPC audit forwarder that: 1) reliably uploads audit blobs to customer-managed storage (S3-compatible and Azure Blob) with multipart/resume and integrity checks; 2) supports customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) via envelope encryption + KMS/HSM reference, with key-rotation metadata annotated per-tenant; 3) exposes admin controls (RBAC v2 enforced) for storage targets and lifecycle policies; and 4) includes throttling/backpressure and durable local buffering to tolerate intermittent connectivity.

Why this work:
- Customers running Redwood Private require push-to-customer-storage for compliance and egress control. Current forwarder implementations lack robust resume, per-tenant CMEK semantics, and lifecycle metadata required by large customers. This ticket consolidates reliability, security, and admin UX needs.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Resilient multipart upload protocol with resume and exponential backoff; verified against large (100GB+) synthetic audit streams.
- Support for S3-compatible endpoints and Azure Blob with a pluggable storage adapter interface.
- Per-tenant envelope encryption where Redwood never holds the plaintext CMK; support both customer KMS endpoints (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and on-prem HSM) and a local envelope-key option for airgapped installs.
- Upload manifests (SHA256 checksums) written alongside blobs for integrity verification and easy reingest.
- Durable on-disk queue with configurable max size and eviction policy; policy-driven fallback to internal encrypted store when customer target is unreachable for > configurable threshold.
- Admin APIs/Console (RBAC v2 enforced) to manage storage endpoints, retention/lifecycle policies, and per-tenant encryption configuration; changes are auditable in the platform audit log.
- Observability: per-tenant metrics (upload success/failure rates, bytes/sec, queue depth), tracing for upload lifecycle, and alerts for sustained failures (SLO: 99.9% successful forward within 1 hour for connected tenants).
- Security review completed and documented; threat model includes key leakage, replay, and forged manifests.

Technical approach:
- Forwarder core: Go service embedded in Private control plane that serializes audit events to chunked files and uploads with a multipart/resume protocol. Uses signed upload sessions and ephemeral upload tokens to avoid long-standing credentials.
- Encryption: Implement envelope encryption where: a) Redwood generates ephemeral data key; b) data key is encrypted by customer CMK (KMS or HSM) using customer-provided key reference; c) ciphertext and key-ref metadata stored with blob. Provide a fallback path for airgapped HSM workflows (customer provides wrapped key material).
- Storage adapters: pluggable interface (S3, S3-compatible, Azure Blob). Adapter responsibilities: multipart lifecycle, presigned URL generation, server-side encryption flags (where applicable), and tagging for lifecycle.
- Local buffering: RocksDB-backed or filesystem-chunked queue with configurable retention. Implement backpressure signals to local producers if queue near capacity. Support high-water/low-water thresholds and TTL-based eviction.
- Throttling & QoS: Per-tenant bandwidth shaping using token-bucket to ensure a noisy customer cannot saturate site egress. Admin-configurable per-tenant rate limits and global burst controls.
- Admin controls & RBAC v2: All storage target CRUD, key configuration, and lifecycle changes go through RBAC v2 checks. UI changes guarded by SSO/SAML group mappings. Changes are versioned and write an audit record to the internal audit sink.

Trade-offs considered:
- Encrypt-at-rest vs. envelope encryption: envelope ensures Redwood never manages long-term CMKs but requires reliable KMS connectivity for rotations. We implement local wrapped-key support to support airgapped customers.
- Local buffer durability: RocksDB adds dependency and complexity; plain file-chunking is simpler. We'll prototype RocksDB for index performance but design interface to swap to file-chunks if needed.
- Immediate failover to internal store vs. delayed retry: chosen policy = immediate retry with exponential backoff + after threshold switch to encrypted internal stash to meet SLA for audit retention.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype adapter + encryption in staging (brownfield integration test with minio and Azure Storage emulator).
2) Internal dogfood in Redwood Private-qa for two customers (one S3-compatible, one Azure).
3) Feature flagged rollout to new Private customers; default off for existing installs.
4) GA when two customers have completed integration and security review signed off.

Testing & Validation:
- Unit tests for adapter interface and encryption codepath.
- Integration tests against MinIO, AWS S3 (dev account), and Azurite.
- Chaos tests: network partition, KMS unavailability, disk fill.
- Performance test: throughput and queue sizing exercises with 10k events/sec.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- Metrics: forwarder_upload_success, forwarder_upload_failure, forwarder_queue_depth, forwarder_bytes_uploaded, forwarder_cmek_rotate_failures.
- Alerts: >5% failure rate over 15m, queue depth > 80% capacity for 30m, KMS error rate spike.

Docs & Customer onboarding:
- Confluence: /confluence/display/INF/OnPrem+Audit+Forwarder+Design (PRD link).
- Customer playbook: step-by-step to configure storage target, KMS integration instructions for AWS/Azure/HSM, and recommended retention policies.
- Console help text for retention and bandwidth controls.

Migration & Backfill:
- Backfill tooling to re-upload locally-stashed audit blobs to new customer targets with checksum verification and dry-run mode.
- Migration plan for customers using existing forwarder: config export/import and small window cutover.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Key leakage risk: mitigate by never persisting plaintext data keys and restricting KMS access scope; require SSO-based admin approval for key refs.
- Large customer upload spikes causing egress costs: provide per-tenant throttles and quota alerts; add cost warnings in console.
- Airgapped install complexity: document explicit manual steps and provide validation tooling.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we expose an API for customers to request re-encryption when they rotate keys, or require Redwood to initiate rewrap during upload? (Pref: expose endpoint + admin-initiated rewrap flow.)
- Which local store implementation do we standardize on for GA (RocksDB vs. file-chunks)? Prototype first; evaluate at POC completion.
